faq.question: After Class 12, are Indian students able to pursue a career in public health in Canada?
faq.answer: Yes,. Applications for bachelor's degrees in public health, health sciences, or health studies are accepted from Indian students. The majority of MPH programs demand a bachelor's degree.

faq.question: Does studying public health in Canada require NEET?
faq.answer: For public health programs, NEET is typically not a prerequisite for entrance. Academic credentials and course-specific admission requirements are used by universities to evaluate applicants.

faq.question: How long does an MPH take in Canada?
faq.answer: Depending on the university, course structure, internship or practicum requirements, and study method, many MPH programs take one to two years.

faq.question: How much does it cost to study public health in Canada?
faq.answer: In general, living expenditures and tuition could come to at least CAD 35,100-90,100 annually. Applicants should refer to official fee schedules as actual costs differ by city and university.

faq.question: After earning an MPH, can I get employment in Canada?
faq.answer: Graduates may seek for pertinent positions in healthcare administration, epidemiology support, research, public health initiatives, and health policy. Qualifications, experience, work authorization, company criteria, and the job market all influence employment. A job or permanent residence are not guaranteed by an MPH alone.
